column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
A cat runs after spotting a mouse and a plant grows towards a window. What do both actions have in common?
You whisper rather than shout when you talk to a friend in class. What does that suggest about how a response is chosen?
When you taste a sweet and then smell a flower, which parts of the body first pick up each of those pieces of information?
Follow a signal inside a single neuron from where it is picked up to where it leaves. Which parts does it pass through, in order?
Two neurons do not touch each other. How can a message still get from one to the next?
After the brain decides to lift an arm, which tissue actually carries out the movement?
What changes inside a muscle cell, at the level of its chemical parts, so that the cell as a whole gets shorter?
Describe in your own words what is common in jumping away from a bus and pulling your hand from a flame.
Where does the quick connection between the sensing nerve and the moving nerve sit, and what does it let the body skip?
If every response had to go through conscious thought, what could go wrong when the situation is dangerous?
Which parts of the body together act as the control room, and what do they do with the signals that arrive?
When you decide to clap, how does the decision travel from where it is made to your hands?
Into how many main regions is the brain divided, and what are they called from front to back?
Describe what happens in the front part of the brain between a sight reaching it and a leg muscle moving in answer.
Which parts of the brain would be affected if a person suddenly could not ride a bicycle straight, and which if their heartbeat and digestion were disturbed?
A helmet works by cushioning a blow. What two layers of cushioning does nature give the brain?
If you run your hand down your back you feel a bumpy ridge. What is it guarding?
When a leaf is touched at its tip, the whole leaf may droop. What must have happened between the touch and the drooping?
Animal muscle cells use special proteins to alter their form. What does a plant cell vary instead to alter its form?
A seedling bends towards a window; a sensitive plant folds when touched. Which of these would stop if growth were prevented, and why?
Describe what happens to the direction of new growth if a plant's shoot is turned away from light for a few days.
A seed sprouts underground in the dark. How do the root and the shoot each know which way to grow?
Name two reasons why a nerve signal alone could not coordinate every cell in a large animal's body.
How does a message sent as a chemical reach a cell with no nerve ending near it, and what is the price of doing it that way?
Plant hormones are not made where they do their work. What does that mean for how they travel?
A window lets light fall on one side of a potted shoot. On which side do the cells end up longer, and what produces that difference?
Plants need hormones to grow and also to stop growing. Which hormones fit each of those two jobs?
Why would a chemical message, rather than only nerve signals, suit a sudden frightening moment?
Describe, organ by organ, how a body changes in the seconds after a real fright and what each change is for.
Salt packets often say 'iodised'. What goes wrong in the neck region if the body gets too little of that ingredient, and why?
Two friends differ greatly in height, and both of you notice changes in your voices and bodies around ten to twelve. Which hormones can explain these two different observations?
A doctor advises a patient to cut down sugar and may prescribe a regular treatment. Which organ's product is short in this patient, and what is it normally responsible for?
After a sugary meal, which organ notices the rise, what does it do, and what happens later when the level comes back down?
Give one way the nervous system and one way hormones help a body control and coordinate what it does.
